CLINICAL DETAILS: 72F. Previous abdominal hysterectomy. 48 hours of colicky abdominal pain, distension and bilious vomiting, not opened bowels for 3 days. ?Obstruction.

TECHNIQUE: CT abdomen and pelvis, portal venous phase, following intravenous contrast.

FINDINGS:
Multiple dilated, fluid-filled small bowel loops measuring up to 38 mm, with a single transition point in the right lower abdomen and no mass at this site, most likely an adhesional band. Small bowel faeces sign just proximal to the transition. The distal ileum and colon are collapsed. No closed loop obstruction. The dilated loops enhance normally with no features to suggest ischaemia. The hernial orifices are clear. The appendix is unremarkable.

The liver, gallbladder and biliary tree are unremarkable.

The pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands are unremarkable.

The kidneys are unremarkable with no hydronephrosis. The bladder is unremarkable.

No free intraperitoneal gas. Small volume of interloop free fluid. No collection.

No lymphadenopathy. The abdominal aorta is of normal calibre with mild atherosclerotic calcification.

Post-hysterectomy. No pelvic mass.

The lung bases are clear. Degenerative change in the lumbar spine. No aggressive bone lesion.

CONCLUSION:
1. Small bowel obstruction with a single transition point in the right lower abdomen, likely adhesional.
2. No closed loop or features of ischaemia.
Recommend surgical review.
